about.name: Kevin Stev Bayer
bio_paragraphs: I'm a Mechatronics Engineering student at KCG College of Technology, Chennai, building intelligent machines at the intersection of software, electronics, and mechanical design. My focus is on autonomous robotics, simulation-driven development, and real-time embedded control — skills I'm actively refining for graduate-level research and industry.

Currently targeting Master's programs in Robotics and Autonomous Systems at TU Munich, ETH Zürich, and KTH Royal Institute of Technology. My portfolio demonstrates hands-on competency in full-stack robotics: from URDF modelling and physics simulation to embedded C++ and ROS2 navigation stacks.

projects.title: Humanoid Sim — Project Titan
projects.short_description: Full-body humanoid simulation in MuJoCo 3.x with Python IK solver, Minimum Jerk trajectory generation, and a 7-step reactive FSM for tabletop manipulation.
projects.full_description: Titan is a full-body articulated humanoid model simulated in MuJoCo 3.x, capable of standing balance, arm-space Cartesian control, and multi-step tabletop manipulation sequences. The control stack is built entirely in Python: a Damped Least Squares IK solver handles Cartesian-to-joint-space mapping with singularity robustness, a Minimum Jerk trajectory generator ensures smooth, dynamically feasible joint motion, and a Reactive FSM sequences the full pick-and-place pipeline across 7 discrete states — from idle through reach, grasp, lift, place, retract, and home — with real-time collision monitoring at each transition. Integrated with ROS2 Humble: joint states are published to /joint_states and a rviz2 launch file brings up the full visualisation in one command.
highlights: MuJoCo 3.x MJCF full-body humanoid model — 22+ DOF simulated at real-time rate
Damped Least Squares (DLS) IK solver with λ-damping for singularity-robust Cartesian arm control
Minimum Jerk trajectory generator producing smooth, physically feasible joint velocity profiles
7-step Reactive FSM: idle → reach → grasp → lift → place → retract → home with collision monitoring
ROS2 Humble bridge: /joint_states publisher + tf2 broadcast, visualised live in rviz2

media.image_alt: Titan Humanoid in MuJoCo 3.x — bipedal robot at tabletop with coloured manipulation targets

projects.title: Project Titan — 3kg Competition UGV
projects.short_description: High-traction 4WD competition UGV. Dual BTS7960 H-bridges, 2200 mAh 80C LiPo, Arduino control loop with RC and serial command modes.
projects.full_description: Project Titan is a 4WD Unmanned Ground Vehicle engineered for the 3 kg competition class. The plywood platform chassis mounts four large-diameter knobby-tread wheels driven by a dual BTS7960 H-bridge array — each module rated for 43 A peak current, making it capable of sustained high-torque output without thermal throttling. A 2200 mAh 80C LiPo pack with XT60 connector delivers the burst current headroom the drivetrain demands. The Arduino Nano control board runs a dual-mode firmware loop: RC receiver input (PWM channel decoding) for direct human piloting and a serial UART command interface for autonomous waypoint commands. All wiring is harnessed with strain relief and secured for vibration tolerance under competition load. Full schematics, firmware, and assembly notes are on GitHub.
highlights: 4WD drivetrain — four DC gearbox motors driven by dual BTS7960 H-bridge modules (43 A peak each)
2200 mAh 80C LiPo power plant with XT60 connector, delivering sustained burst current under max load
Arduino Nano dual-mode firmware: RC PWM receiver input + serial UART autonomous command interface
Plywood platform chassis — tuned mass distribution for low centre-of-gravity traction performance
Full schematics, firmware source, and build notes documented on GitHub

media.image_alt: Project Titan 3kg UGV — 4WD competition robot with 2200mAh LiPo and dual BTS7960 drivers

projects.title: Mechatronics Lab — C++ Firmware Library
projects.short_description: A structured C++ library of embedded systems experiments — PID controllers, interrupt-driven encoder reading, sensor drivers, and a lightweight MCU hardware abstraction layer.
projects.full_description: mechatronics-lab is an evolving C++ firmware repository built around Arduino and AVR microcontroller targets, capturing hands-on embedded systems work accumulated across multiple projects. The library is structured into self-contained modules: a software PID controller with anti-windup clamping; an interrupt-driven quadrature encoder reader for accurate RPM and position feedback; I2C sensor drivers for MPU6050 (6-DOF IMU), HC-SR04 (ultrasonic range), and IR sensor arrays; a PWM motor control abstraction compatible with L298N and BTS7960 H-bridge wiring; and a lightweight hardware abstraction layer (HAL) that allows the same controller logic to run across different MCU variants with minimal porting effort. All modules are commented, serial-debug-instrumented, and MIT-licensed.
highlights: PID module with configurable Kp/Ki/Kd, anti-windup integral clamping, and derivative-on-measurement
Interrupt-driven quadrature encoder driver — accurate RPM + position at 100 Hz sample rate
I2C sensor drivers: MPU6050 (gyro + accel), HC-SR04 (ultrasonic), TCRT5000 IR array (8-ch)
PWM motor abstraction: unified API for L298N and BTS7960 H-bridge configurations
MIT-licensed, fully commented firmware — intended as a reusable personal embedded toolkit

media.image_alt: Mechatronics lab firmware — embedded C++ experiments and sensor drivers

projects.title: Autonomous Line-Following Robot
projects.short_description: 8-sensor IR array differential-drive robot with cascaded PID line-tracking and ultrasonic obstacle-avoidance FSM. Sub-5 mm path deviation at competition speed.
projects.full_description: A differential-drive autonomous robot using an 8-channel TCRT5000 IR sensor array for high-resolution line detection. The control architecture uses a cascaded PID loop — the outer loop computes a weighted positional centroid error across all 8 sensors, the inner loop maps that error to differential PWM commands on both drive motors via an L298N H-bridge. A secondary ultrasonic FSM overlays obstacle detection: when an obstacle is detected within 15 cm the robot exits line-follow mode, executes a 3-step navigation-around manoeuvre, and re-acquires the line through a scan-and-pivot recovery. Gains were tuned iteratively on a 20 mm black-tape course; final tuned values (Kp=1.8, Ki=0.02, Kd=0.9) produce a sub-5 mm steady-state path deviation at full competition speed.
highlights: 8-channel TCRT5000 IR array sampled at 100 Hz via Arduino timer interrupt — low-latency line detection
Cascaded PID: weighted centroid outer loop → differential PWM inner loop (Kp=1.8, Ki=0.02, Kd=0.9)
Obstacle-avoidance FSM: line_follow → detect → navigate_around → re_acquire in under 2 s total
Sub-5 mm steady-state deviation on 20 mm black tape at full competition speed

media.image_alt: Autonomous line-following robot with 8-channel IR sensor array

projects.title: ROS2 Sensor Fusion Node
projects.short_description: ROS2 Humble node fusing RPLidar A1 scans and MPU6050 IMU via complementary filter into a fused pose estimate + 2D occupancy grid, visualised live in rviz2.
projects.full_description: A custom ROS2 (Humble) package implementing sensor fusion for 2D ground-robot localisation. The node subscribes to /scan (RPLidar A1 LaserScan) and /imu/data (MPU6050 over I2C to Raspberry Pi), applies a complementary filter (α=0.98) to fuse scan-derived yaw with raw gyroscope heading for drift-free orientation estimation, and publishes the fused pose on /odom with a full tf2 broadcast tree (map → odom → base_link) at 50 Hz. A 2D occupancy grid is built in real-time from scan data and published at 5 Hz on /map, rendered live in rviz2. The package is designed as the localisation backbone for a future Nav2 navigation stack integration.
highlights: Complementary filter (α=0.98) fuses RPLidar scan-match yaw with IMU gyroscope — drift-free heading
Full tf2 tree: map → odom → base_link broadcast at 50 Hz via TransformBroadcaster
Real-time 2D occupancy grid at 5 Hz on /map, rendered live in rviz2 with colour-mapped probability
Single ros2 launch file starts Lidar driver, IMU node, fusion node, and rviz2 simultaneously

media.image_alt: ROS2 sensor fusion rviz2 — fused pose and 2D occupancy grid

projects.title: Industrial Arm — KUKA KR10 Path Planning
projects.short_description: Planned project: collision-free offline programming for KUKA KR10 R1100 via KRL and RoboDK, with digital twin verification before physical deployment.
projects.full_description: Upcoming industrial robotics project targeting the full offline programming workflow for the KUKA KR10 R1100 six-axis arm. The plan covers CAD model import into RoboDK, reach-envelope analysis, collision-free path generation via OMPL (RRT-Connect) through the RoboDK Python API, KRL script export to the KRC4 controller, and a digital twin validation cycle before any physical robot motion. The project will document a reusable template for academic-to-industry knowledge transfer in industrial manipulator programming, covering both pick-and-place and weld-seam-tracking workflows.
highlights: KUKA KR10 R1100 — 6-DOF industrial arm, 10 kg payload, ±0.05 mm positional repeatability
Full offline programming workflow: RoboDK import → reach analysis → path generation → KRL export
OMPL RRT-Connect collision-free path planning integrated via RoboDK Python API
Digital twin validation loop — full simulation run required before any physical robot motion
